**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, leather-bound book—a single sheet of yellowed paper, brittle at the edges. The handwriting was familiar, though the name at the top was crossed out. My fingers traced the ink, slow and deliberate, as if the words themselves were alive.

*"Dearest [Name],"*

*"I don’t know how to say this without breaking something inside me. I’ve been thinking about you for years, and I don’t know if I can live without you. The world feels too big, too empty without you in it. I don’t know if I can do this. I don’t know if I can."*

The rest was smudged, as if the writer had hesitated, then torn it away. I flipped the page, expecting more, but there was nothing. Just the faint scent of aged paper and something else—something like regret.

I closed the book, my heart pounding. Who had written this? To whom? And why had they left it here, in a place where no one would ever find it?

I didn’t know. But I knew I had to keep it.

Because some letters aren’t meant to be read. But some are meant to be saved.
